newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi says EMU goal is within Italy's reach.
newsitem.headline: Prodi says EMU goal is within Italy's reach.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Thursday that Italy's goal to be in the first wave of European Monetary Union was "within our reach".

"The objective that we have followed is that of putting Italy in the condition to be among the first (countries) in the single European currency," he said in a speech to a business association in Rome.
"Today, this objective is within our reach," he said.
"The country is engaged in a great effort to get public spending in order and this has required sacrifices from our citizens that have not been small," he said.
"Certainly, we have to keep the helm straight on the course that we have assigned ourselves and there is still much to do but the course we have set out on has given us comforting results," he added.
Prodi has been consistently optimistic in recent months about Italy's chances of joining Europe's planned economic and monetary union at its scheduled launch in 1999.

Analysts believe Italy's chances have been boosted by recent political developments in Europe, with both Germany and France struggling to reduce their budget deficits to three percent of gross domestic product, a target in the Maastricht Treaty for euro aspirants.
Italy is also committed to cutting its deficit to three percent of GDP from 6.7 percent last year.
Prodi's centre-left government has launched a wide-ranging review of the welfare state with trade unions and employers, and hopes to introduce a reform of social spending in the 1998 budget.
Analysts say reform is vital if Italy is to keep its state accounts balanced in the years ahead. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
